speaker: Doctor
text: Please tell me your age and weight, and do these breathing sounds happen only when you are eating or lying on your back?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of stridor worsening with neck flexion and feeding-related vomiting, I need to evaluate for vascular rings or laryngeal compression. REQUEST TEST: Barium_Swallow; REQUEST IMAGES: Laryngoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Barium_Swallow findings show compression of the esophagus and trachea consistent with a vascular ring. REQUESTED IMAGE: Laryngoscopy results are not available in the provided data; please note that the Barium Swallow findings strongly support the clinical suspicion of a vascular ring (specifically a double aortic arch confirmed by other tests) rather than isolated laryngeal compression.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Born full term with no complications during birth. Social history: First child in the family. Lives with both parents. No exposure to smoking or pets in the household.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, diarrhea, rash, or other respiratory symptoms such as cough. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis is not a diagnosis for a 10-month-old infant; based on the stridor worsening with neck flexion and vomiting after feeding, this is highly suggestive of Laryngomalacia or a Vascular Ring. I will proceed with the requested Barium Swallow and Laryngoscopy images to confirm the anatomical cause.
